content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash (yellow or green) is a young, tender variety of zucchini harvested before full maturity. It has a soft texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and a bright color. It is commonly sautéed in a small amount of oil to retain its moisture and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash belongs to the cucurbit family and is closely related to cucumbers and pumpkins.
The yellow and green types differ only in pigment; their nutritional profiles are virtually identical.
It is about 95 % water, making it very low in calories.
Easy to grow in greenhouses or open fields, it can be harvested in 50‑60 days.
Culinary uses include French‑style sauté, stews, casseroles, and gratins.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: One cup of sliced summer squash provides roughly 20 kcal, ideal for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports immune function and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Yellow squash is especially high in beta‑carotene, a provitamin A.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to cucurbit vegetables.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic squash, rinse thoroughly to reduce pesticide exposure.

items.title: Excess sodium
items.content: Adding too much salt during cooking can offset the vegetable’s health benefits.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the squash into rounds or half‑moons and quickly sauté in vegetable oil until lightly golden. It can be added to salads, stews, pasta dishes, omelets, and casseroles. Serve the dish promptly to retain its crisp texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep summer squash in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a paper towel or a perforated bag. Stored properly, it stays fresh for 3‑5 days. Avoid storing it with ethylene‑producing fruits.
